objectives.statement: Distinguish deontic modal meaning from epistemic modal meaning in common Norwegian modal verbs.
Select må, kan, skal, vil, and bør to express obligation, permission, intention, probability, and advice.
Use jo, vel, nok, and da to adjust certainty, shared assumption, probability, and emphasis.
Avoid overloading one sentence with too many modal and stance markers.

notes: High-risk modal-meaning topic. Keep as a standalone lesson because it contrasts deontic obligation/permission/intention with epistemic inference/probability/reported expectation in må, skal, kan, vil, and bør. Mention jo, vel, nok, and da only as small particles that modify modal force; do not duplicate the full source/commitment system from hedging_stance_markers or the broader discourse-pragmatic work of advanced_pragmatics.
